newsitem.title: USA: Kimberly-Clark to sell three pulp mills.
newsitem.headline: Kimberly-Clark to sell three pulp mills.

text.p: Kimberly-Clark Corp said it was getting out of the stand-alone pulp business by selling three mills in Ontario, Nova Scotia and Spain and expects to get at least $600 million from the sales.

The Dallas-based consumer products company said in a statement it intends to sell its pulp operations and related woodlands at Terrace Bay in Ontario, New Glasgow in Nova Scotia and Miranda, Spain by mid-1998.
The company is already in the process of selling its pulp operation in Coosa Pines, Ala., to Montreal-based Alliance Forest Products for about $600 million in cash.
Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Wayne R. Sanders told Reuters he expects the new sales to bring in revenue of at least $600 million.
"We would estimate we could get at least as much as we are getting for Coosa for these other three facilities. In total, at least $600 million," he said in a telephone interview.

The three mills produce only pulp and Sanders said Kimberly- Clark wanted to get out of the cyclical, capital-intensive business in order to "redeploy the capital into higher-returning investments for our shareholders."

"Having this much capital tied up in a commodity price business with high capital intensity is not consistent with our strategy of being a consumer products company and we think we can better redeploy the capital elsewhere," Sanders said.

He said Kimberly-Clark would retain its pulp and recycled fiber operations in Everett, Wash. and Mobile, Ala. Those two plants produce the Scott line of consumer tissues, napkins and hand towels and Kimberly-Clark's "away-from-home" products such as handwipes and roll towels.
The sale of the three plants means Kimberly-Clark would buy pulp on the open market for its Kleenex tissue products.
Kimberly-Clark also said it plans to write down certain pulp assets tand to close its Mohave converting mill in Yucca, Ariz.
It said the sale of the Coosa Pines mill and the costs associated with write-downs and the closure of the Mohave operation would bring a net gain of 7 cents per share in the first quarter of 1997.

Internal pulp operations currently meet about 80 percent of Kimberly-clark's worldwide virgin fiber needs and Sanders said that number would drop to below 30 percent with the sale of the Coose Pines operation and the stand-alone mills.
